question.text: For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></math>, where '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math>' is a constant. If percentage error in measurement of  '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>' and '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>' are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo>%</mo></math>, respectively, then the percentage error for '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math>' will be _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math>.

solution.text:
Given: z=a2x3y12

Relative error is given by 

∆zz=3×∆xx+12×∆yy

Now, maximum percentage error in z is 

∆zz×100=34+122×100

=18%.
